note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables (34 alates, 20 workers), figure numbers, synonymic citations and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Rather similar to some forms of A. brevior, the differences being discussed under that species. The development of the postclypeus and its median suture varies markedly, most obviously in the worker and reflected in the corresponding alates: forest specimens have the weakest postclypeal development and the alates often lack a median suture, whereas savanna forms have a well-developed postclypeus and median suture.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white; pilosity pale yellow, sparse, inconspicuous. Postclypeus weakly to strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.24–0.35, Pcl/Ry 1.89–2.97; mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.43–0.54, Ra/Ri 0.57–0.76; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 7.25–11.41; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin only half that of the second marginal tooth or shorter, Ra/Ri·Rm 9.94–13.08. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 4.21–5.52; third apical spur distinct, about one third the length of the other two. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is dorsal, weakly bilobed, sessile or attached to the second hindgut pouch, or with a very short neck; the valve membrane bears sparse minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, very dark above the ocelli. Fontanelle variable, from broadly elliptical and nearly circular to elongate-elliptical, distinctly smaller than to as large as the ocellus, slightly raised, flat or slightly concave, from conspicuous yellowish white to dark brown only slightly paler than the head capsule; most commonly elliptical, smaller than the ocellus, slightly concave and paler than the head capsule. Central spot circular to elongate-elliptical, reduced to slightly smaller than the fontanelle, flat or slightly raised, concolorous with the head capsule. Postclypeus brown to dark brown, labrum pale brown, antennae brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum brown, usually with a dark transverse suture; femora brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles dark brown, sternites brown with a yellow median area, ventral spiracles brown; cerci yellowish white to pale brown. Posterior margin of head capsule undulate, rarely nearly evenly rounded; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye from one quarter of their minimum diameter to slightly less than the minimum diameter; postclypeus very weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.18–0.27, Pcl/Ra 2.06–3.48, posterior margin mostly evenly rounded, sometimes arcuate, median suture often weak or absent. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.42–0.55, Ra/Rj 0.55–0.74; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin distinctly shorter than that of the second. Cephalic pilosity brown, the short hairs forming an even layer, with longer outstanding setae scattered among them. Meso- and metanotum broader at the constriction, M/W 0.26–0.34. Third apical spur of the fore tibia short but distinct.
